Let's analyze the options:

A. "Very few books are banned but an exception is a book by Jean Martin." — This is vague and doesn't specify which book. Also, "Jean Martin" is not a well-known author in the context of Irish book bans.

B. "Books banned in Ireland include Catcher in the Rye, Brave New World and Ulysses." — This is inaccurate. While Ireland had a history of banning books, most of these bans have been lifted. "Catcher in the Rye" and "Brave New World" were never officially banned in Ireland. "Ulysses" was banned for a time but is no longer banned.

C. "Catcher in the Rye by J.D. Salinger is banned." — This is incorrect. "Catcher in the Rye" was never banned in Ireland.

D. "Balzac." — This is too vague. Some works by Balzac were banned in the past, but not currently.

E. "Borstal Boy." — This book by Brendan Behan was banned in Ireland for a time, but the ban was lifted in 1970.

F. "Ulysses by James Joyce." — "Ulysses" was banned in Ireland from 1922 until the 1960s, but it is no longer banned.

Given the current state of Irish censorship, almost no books are banned today. The only answer that is close to being correct, in the sense that it acknowledges the rarity of bans and mentions a specific (though obscure) exception, is A. However, the reference to "Jean Martin" is questionable and not supported by historical records.

None of the options are fully correct, but A is the least incorrect, as it at least acknowledges that very few books are banned.

Answer: A
